chapters.summary: David learns that Saul and Jonathan have died in battle, and he mourns their deaths while punishing the Amalekite who falsely claimed to have killed the king.
keyPoints: David hears the news of Saul's death from an Amalekite who claims to have killed him.
David and his men tear their clothes, fast, and weep, grieving deeply for Saul and Jonathan.
David puts the Amalekite to death for killing the LORD's anointed, and composes a lament mourning Saul and Jonathan.
chapters.application: When we lose a loved one or a leader, let us face it with honesty and integrity, honoring them through our grief, and let this teach us to trust in the sovereignty of God.

chapters.summary: David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron, while Ish-bosheth is made king over Israel, and the rivalry between the two houses leads to war and the death of Abner.
keyPoints: David inquires of the LORD, goes up to Hebron, and is anointed king by the men of Judah.
Abner makes Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, king over Israel, setting the north against the south.
The two sides clash at the pool of Gibeon, where Abner kills Asahel, and the conflict widens.
chapters.application: When facing life's decisions, let us first inquire of the LORD and trust his leading, and even amid conflict, let us seek peace and reconciliation.

chapters.summary: War continues between the house of David and the house of Saul; Abner defects to David but is killed in an act of revenge by Joab, and David mourns his death.
keyPoints: David's house grows stronger and stronger, while Saul's house grows weaker.
Rebuked by Ish-bosheth, Abner defects to David, seeking to bring all Israel over to him.
To avenge his brother, Joab treacherously kills Abner, and David publicly mourns him to make clear his own innocence.
chapters.application: In conflict and grievance, let us follow David's example, leaving judgment to God and handling relationships with grace and integrity rather than acting out of anger or revenge.

chapters.summary: Saul's son Ish-bosheth is murdered by two of his own army commanders; when David learns of it, he executes the killers and gives Ish-bosheth an honorable burial.
keyPoints: Weak and powerless, Ish-bosheth is assassinated by his own officers, Baanah and Rechab.
The killers bring his head to David expecting a reward, but David has them severely punished instead.
David's righteous response shows his reverence for the one the LORD had anointed as king.
chapters.application: Let us follow David's example, refusing to act rashly out of impulse, leaving judgment to God, and conducting ourselves with justice and reverence.

chapters.summary: David is anointed king over all Israel at Hebron, captures Jerusalem, and defeats the Philistines.
keyPoints: All the tribes of Israel come to Hebron, make a covenant with David, and anoint him king over all Israel.
David captures the stronghold of Jerusalem from the Jebusites, makes it his capital, and grows steadily stronger.
The Philistines attack twice, and David inquires of the LORD and defeats them according to his instruction.
chapters.application: Let us inquire of God in all things rather than act on our own judgment, and he will lead us to victory.

chapters.summary: David brings the ark up to Jerusalem; along the way Uzzah is struck down by God for touching it, David is afraid but later rejoices as the ark is brought in, and Michal despises David and is punished.
keyPoints: David leads a grand procession to bring up the ark, but carries it on a new cart instead of by the manner God prescribed.
Uzzah reaches out to steady the ark and is struck down by God; David becomes afraid and leaves the ark at the house of Obed-edom.
The ark brings blessing to Obed-edom's household, so David brings it up with rejoicing, but Michal despises him for leaping and dancing, and she remains childless to the end.
chapters.application: Let us worship God with reverent hearts, doing things his way rather than treating his holiness lightly. In worship, let us hold on to joy and humility, seeking only to please God rather than to satisfy the eyes of others.

chapters.summary: David wants to build a house for God, but instead God promises to establish David's house and kingdom, and makes an everlasting covenant with him.
keyPoints: Having been given rest by God, David wishes to build him a temple, but God sends word through the prophet Nathan.
God reminds David that he brought Israel out of Egypt without ever asking for a temple to be built, and promises to appoint a place for his people.
God makes a covenant with David, promising that his offspring will succeed him on the throne and that his kingdom will be established forever.
chapters.application: God values our hearts more than our outward offerings. Let us submit humbly, allowing God to accomplish his plans in his own way, and trust in his promises.

chapters.summary: David defeats the surrounding nations—the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, and Syria—taking great amounts of silver, gold, and bronze, and appoints officials to govern the kingdom, so that it grows strong.
keyPoints: David defeats the Philistines, capturing Gath and other towns, and subdues this formidable enemy.
David defeats Moab, Hadadezer king of Zobah, and the Syrians, expanding his territory.
David dedicates the plunder to the LORD and governs Israel with justice.
chapters.application: When we experience success in life, let us remember to give the glory to God, following David's example of ruling justly and serving others with grateful hearts.

chapters.summary: Remembering his covenant with Jonathan, David shows kindness to Saul's descendant Mephibosheth, restoring Saul's land to him and inviting him to always eat at the king's table.
keyPoints: David seeks out anyone left of Saul's house, so that for Jonathan's sake he may show kindness to Mephibosheth.
David restores Saul's land to Mephibosheth and appoints Ziba to manage the property and serve him.
Mephibosheth eats regularly at David's table like one of the king's sons, displaying God's faithfulness and grace.
chapters.application: Let us follow David's example, showing kindness to those who can never repay us, for God first showed us grace, bringing us to his table and giving us the status of his own children.

chapters.summary: David defeats the combined forces of the Ammonites and the Syrians, displaying God's presence and David's victory.
keyPoints: David sends envoys to comfort Hanun, king of the Ammonites, but they are disgraced instead, sparking a war.
The Ammonites hire Syrian mercenaries, and David sends Joab and Abishai out to fight, winning a great victory.
The Syrians regroup, and David personally leads the army to defeat them, causing the nations to submit.
chapters.application: When we face misunderstanding or hostility, let us follow David's example, relying on God and facing it with courage, for he will be with us and grant us victory.

chapters.summary: While Uriah is away at war, David commits adultery with Bathsheba and arranges for Uriah's death, revealing the seriousness of sin and the certainty of God's judgment.
keyPoints: Walking on the roof of his palace, David sees Bathsheba bathing, sends for her, and sleeps with her.
When Bathsheba becomes pregnant, David tries to get Uriah to go home to cover up the sin, but Uriah remains loyal and will not go.
David has Uriah killed by the hand of the enemy and takes Bathsheba as his wife, and the LORD is greatly displeased by what he has done.
chapters.application: Let us be watchful against temptation in seasons of ease and comfort, and never abuse the authority we are given. When we sin, let us repent at once rather than compounding one wrong with another, for God sees everything.

chapters.summary: The prophet Nathan confronts David over his sin with Bathsheba, David repents, but God still pronounces judgment—the child dies, and Solomon is born.
keyPoints: Nathan exposes David's sin through a parable; David grows furious at the man in the story, not realizing he is condemning himself.
David confesses and repents, and God forgives his sin, yet declares that the sword will never leave his house and that the child will die.
David fasts and pleads for the sick child, and after the child dies he rises and worships; God then gives him Solomon, and the LORD loves him.
chapters.application: When our sin is exposed, let us humbly accept it and repent sincerely, trusting in God's forgiveness while still bearing the consequences of sin, and begin again in his grace.

chapters.summary: David's son Amnon violates his sister Tamar, Absalom avenges her by killing Amnon, and calamity after calamity befalls David's household.
keyPoints: Amnon feigns illness to lure Tamar into caring for him, then takes the opportunity to violate her.
After Tamar is disgraced, Absalom comforts her while secretly planning revenge.
Absalom arranges a feast and kills Amnon; David is grief-stricken, and Absalom flees to Geshur.
chapters.application: When harm occurs within a family, let us seek God's wisdom and forgiveness rather than repaying evil with evil, and let God heal what is broken.

chapters.summary: Joab arranges for a wise woman of Tekoa to persuade David, so that Absalom is allowed to return from Geshur, but David still refuses to see him.
keyPoints: Sensing that David longs for Absalom, Joab devises a plan to send the woman of Tekoa to move David with a parable.
Using her own supposed situation as a parallel to David's family, the woman leads David to acknowledge that he ought to receive Absalom back.
David allows Absalom to return to Jerusalem but will not see his face for two full years.
chapters.application: In family conflict, let us seek reconciliation with wisdom, following God's example of mercy and taking the initiative to mend broken relationships.

chapters.summary: Absalom wins over the hearts of the people of Israel through cunning, and then revolts and proclaims himself king at Hebron, forcing David to flee Jerusalem.
keyPoints: Absalom courts the people's favor, feigning concern for those who come to him with a dispute, and steals away the hearts of Israel.
Absalom declares himself king at Hebron, and upon hearing the news David decides to flee Jerusalem.
David departs with his officials and his people, leaving ten concubines to keep the palace, and sends the priests Zadok and Abiathar back.
chapters.application: When facing betrayal and hardship, let us follow David's example, entrusting sovereignty to God and trusting his leading and promises even in adversity.

chapters.summary: As David flees, he is deceived by Ziba and cursed by Shimei, yet he chooses to bear it patiently and trusts in God's will.
keyPoints: Ziba wins David's trust through gifts and lies, and gains Mephibosheth's property for himself.
Shimei curses David, but David stops Abishai from taking revenge, seeing it as something the LORD has permitted.
Absalom enters Jerusalem, and with Ahithophel's counsel offered, David's crisis deepens.
chapters.application: When we face injustice or disgrace, let us learn David's patience, leaving judgment to God, trusting firmly that he is watching over us, and holding on to faith in adversity.

chapters.summary: Ahithophel proposes a plan to hunt down David, but Hushai's counsel undermines it, allowing David to escape and learn that Absalom's cause will fail.
keyPoints: Ahithophel advises pursuing and killing David that very night, but Absalom does not act on it right away.
Pretending loyalty to Absalom, Hushai proposes a seemingly safer plan, secretly undoing Ahithophel's counsel.
On receiving word, David crosses the Jordan that same night, escaping Absalom's pursuit.
chapters.application: When others plot against us with cunning, God is still sovereign over all. Let us trust him and seek his guidance in danger, for he will always provide a way through.

chapters.summary: Absalom's rebellion is crushed by David's army, Absalom is killed by Joab, and David is overcome with grief at the news.
keyPoints: David musters his troops and sends them out to battle, instructing them not to harm Absalom.
Absalom's hair catches in the branches of a tree, and Joab, defying the king's command, kills him.
On hearing of Absalom's death, David weeps bitterly and mourns, and the people try to comfort him.
chapters.application: In our own grief, let us remember that God is just, and let us also forgive in love, entrusting the outcome to the Lord, that we may find comfort and peace.

chapters.summary: David mourns Absalom's death and is rebuked by Joab; he then returns to the city and shows mercy toward those who had rebelled—Shimei and Mephibosheth are pardoned, and Barzillai is blessed.
keyPoints: David weeps for Absalom, and Joab rebukes him for neglecting the morale of the army.
David returns to Jerusalem, and when Shimei begs forgiveness, David pardons him.
Mephibosheth explains why he did not go with David, and David divides the land between him and Ziba; Barzillai then takes his leave.
chapters.application: Even in our grief, let us remember the responsibilities we still carry; and let us follow David's example of forgiveness, laying down grudges and pursuing peace with kindness toward others.

chapters.summary: Sheba's rebellion is put down by Joab, securing David's kingdom, but Joab's ruthlessness comes to light once again.
keyPoints: Sheba, a Benjamite, stirs up Israel to desert David, and only the tribe of Judah remains loyal to him.
David sends Amasa to muster the men of Judah, but when Amasa delays, David sends Abishai and Joab after Sheba instead.
Joab kills Amasa at Gibeon, captures the city of Abel, and Sheba is killed, ending the revolt.
chapters.application: When facing division and betrayal, let us act with wisdom and resolve to preserve peace, while remaining watchful about whether our own methods are right, asking God for justice joined with mercy.

chapters.summary: David deals with the Gibeonites' claim for justice and fights against the descendants of the Philistine giants, displaying God's justice and faithfulness.
keyPoints: David hands over Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites to atone for the bloodguilt of Saul's broken oath.
David gives the bones of Saul and Jonathan an honorable burial, and the land is blessed as a result.
David's mighty men strike down the Philistine giants, displaying God's presence and power.
chapters.application: Let us keep our promises, be willing to take responsibility for past wrongs, and rely on God's power to face our challenges, for he will grant justice and peace.

chapters.summary: Delivered from Saul and from all his enemies, David sings a song praising God, celebrating his salvation, protection, and justice.
keyPoints: David expresses his gratitude to God in song, calling him his rock, his deliverer, and his high tower.
The song describes God's majesty appearing in earthquake, fire, and storm, revealing his mighty power.
David declares that God rewards according to righteousness and purity, and that he grants David strength and victory.
chapters.application: Whatever hardship we face, let us follow David's example, crying out to God in song and prayer, trusting his salvation and justice, for he will be our rock and our shield.

chapters.summary: Near the end of his life David praises God in song and records the names and exploits of his mighty men, displaying God's faithfulness and human loyalty.
keyPoints: David rules in righteousness and reverence for God, like the light of morning shining forth.
God makes an everlasting covenant with David, and declares that the wicked will be cast away.
The chapter records thirty-seven mighty men, showing how God accomplishes great things through people.
chapters.application: Whatever our position, let us serve God with loyalty and courage, trusting his promises, and live out an extraordinary testimony even in ordinary places.

chapters.summary: Out of pride David takes a census of the people, bringing God's punishment upon them, but after he buys land, builds an altar, and offers sacrifice, the plague is stopped.
keyPoints: David takes a census of the people and afterward is stricken with remorse, confessing that he has sinned against God.
God sends a plague, and David pleads for mercy, asking to bear the punishment himself.
David buys a threshing floor, builds an altar, and offers sacrifice, and the plague is stopped, displaying God's grace.
chapters.application: In times of prosperity, let us be watchful against pride, inquiring of God in all things, relying on him with humility, and repenting quickly so as to experience his forgiveness and grace.
